moments.title: Pasteur on wine spoilage
moments.body: Pasteur demonstrates that fermenting microbes cause both wine production and its spoilage. Mild heating preserves the wine.
moments.takeaway: Microbiology entered the food supply through wine before milk.

moments.title: Chicago mandates pasteurised milk
moments.body: Chicago becomes one of the first major cities to require pasteurisation, addressing high infant mortality from bovine tuberculosis.
moments.takeaway: Public-health regulation drove the adoption of food technologies.

moments.title: Aseptic packaging at Tetra Pak
moments.who: Erik Wallenberg and Ruben Rausing, Sweden
moments.body:
Wallenberg conceptualises a tetrahedral aseptic carton; Tetra Pak is founded in 1951.

The technology enables ambient-storage milk distribution decades later.
moments.takeaway: Packaging is itself a food technology with supply-chain consequences.

now.title: Food safety today
now.body: HACCP frameworks (1960s onwards), refrigeration audits and DNA-based pathogen detection coexist. Outbreaks like cyclospora and listeria still drive recall regulation.
now.open_questions: How should food safety regulation handle decentralised producers and new ingredient categories such as cultured meat?

items.reflection: Each generation of food technology solves earlier problems and creates new questions about regulation and equity.

moments.title: Appert's canning
moments.body: Appert wins a French government prize for preserving food in heated glass jars. Peter Durand patents the tin can the same year.
moments.takeaway: Military logistics drove early preservation innovation.

moments.title: Birdseye flash freezing
moments.body: Birdseye develops fast freezing techniques after observing Inuit ice-fishing practices in Labrador. General Foods commercialises the method.
moments.takeaway: Field observation and engineering produced household-scale frozen food.

moments.title: Domestic refrigeration takes off
moments.body:
Post-war domestic refrigerator adoption climbs above 80% of US households by the mid-1950s.

UK adoption follows in subsequent decades.
moments.takeaway: Cold storage in the home altered weekly shopping and household labour.

now.title: Cold chain today
now.body: Global cold-chain logistics underpin perishable trade and vaccine distribution. Energy use and refrigerant leakage are climate concerns.
now.open_questions: How should low-emission cooling be deployed in regions with weak grids?

items.reflection: Preservation technologies have reshaped not just food but who does what work in households.

moments.title: Silent Spring
moments.body:
Carson's book on synthetic pesticide use is widely credited with launching the modern environmental movement.

It accelerates the organic movement's public profile.
moments.takeaway: A single book transformed food production debates.

moments.title: IFOAM founded
moments.body: The International Federation of Organic Agriculture Movements (IFOAM) is established to coordinate standards.
moments.takeaway: Voluntary standards preceded national legal frameworks.

moments.title: USDA Organic seal in effect
moments.body: The National Organic Program standardises labelling in the US, following EU regulation 2092/91 in Europe.
moments.takeaway: Certification turned a movement into a regulated market category.

now.title: Organic and beyond
now.body: Organic remains a small but stable share of food sales. Regenerative agriculture, agroecology and precision farming offer overlapping but distinct approaches.
now.open_questions: How should different sustainability claims be comparably measured? What is the right balance between yield and ecosystem services?

items.reflection: Food system change requires both new technologies and new institutional standards to label and price what they produce.

moments.title: Umami isolated
moments.body: Ikeda identifies glutamate as the source of the 'umami' taste, leading to MSG production.
moments.takeaway: Food technology often follows the isolation of specific molecules from traditional ingredients.

moments.title: Quorn commercialised
moments.body: Mycoprotein from Fusarium venenatum, identified by Rank Hovis McDougall in the 1960s, reaches consumers as Quorn after extensive safety testing.
moments.takeaway: Decades of regulatory work preceded a familiar grocery product.

moments.title: First cultured-meat burger tasted
moments.body:
A cultured beef patty costing around $325,000 to produce is cooked and tasted live.

Approval for limited commercial cultured chicken sales follows in Singapore (2020) and the US (2023).
moments.takeaway: Novel foods follow long technology cost curves before reaching shelves.

now.title: Novel proteins today
now.body: Plant-based, fermentation-based and cellular agriculture products compete with conventional meat and dairy. Regulatory frameworks differ by jurisdiction.
now.open_questions: What lifecycle outcomes do novel proteins deliver at scale? How should they be labelled?

items.reflection: What counts as 'food' is being negotiated by regulators, supermarkets and consumers in real time.

moments.title: Wheat domestication
moments.body: Emmer and einkorn wheat are domesticated in the region around modern Iraq, Syria and Turkey.
moments.takeaway: The agricultural revolution made cities possible.

moments.title: Potato in the Andes
moments.body: The potato is domesticated in highland Peru, later spreading globally through 16th-century Spanish trade.
moments.takeaway: The world's staple crops have specific geographic origins.

moments.title: Rice cultivation
moments.body: Rice domestication in southern China feeds the largest sustained populations in human history.
moments.takeaway: Three crops (wheat, rice, maize) now feed most of humanity.

now.title: Crop diversity today
now.body: Svalbard Global Seed Vault (opened 2008) preserves genetic diversity. Three crops still dominate global calorie supply.
now.open_questions: Can monoculture-dependent food systems survive climate change?

items.reflection: Most of what we eat was bred over thousands of years before written history.

moments.title: Salt as preservation
moments.body: Salt becomes a preservative across cultures, enabling stored fish, meat and vegetables.
moments.takeaway: Salt is among the oldest food technologies.

moments.title: Smoking and curing
moments.body: Wood smoke preserves meat and fish by drying surfaces and depositing antimicrobials.
moments.takeaway: Preservation methods evolved long before microbiology explained them.

moments.title: Domesday salt records
moments.body: Domesday Book records salt-producing 'wiches' across England, showing salt's strategic importance.
moments.takeaway: Medieval economies revolved around preservation.

now.title: Salt and health
now.body: Excess salt is linked to hypertension. UK salt reduction in processed food (2003-2011) saved an estimated 9,000 deaths a year.
now.open_questions: How do we balance preservation needs with health risks?

items.reflection: A mineral once worth its weight in gold is now too cheap to notice.

moments.title: Nestle's infant milk
moments.body: Nestle develops a 'farine lactee' for infants whose mothers cannot breastfeed.
moments.takeaway: Industrial food began with medical-style claims.

moments.title: Heinz founded
moments.body: Heinz markets bottled horseradish in clear glass to display its purity, then expands to ketchup and beans.
moments.takeaway: Packaging visibility was an early food-safety argument.

moments.title: Cornflakes invented
moments.body: Kellogg creates flaked cereal at a sanitarium. His brother Will markets them commercially.
moments.takeaway: Breakfast cereal began as health food.

now.title: Big food today
now.body: A handful of multinationals control most processed food. Marketing of ultra-processed food faces growing regulation.
now.open_questions: How do we redirect a food system built for shelf life to one built for health?

items.reflection: The brands we shop with were mostly invented within a couple of decades around 1880.

moments.title: Lind's scurvy trial
moments.body: Lind conducts what is sometimes called the first controlled clinical trial, showing citrus cures scurvy.
moments.takeaway: Trial methodology can predate the disease theory it tests.

moments.title: Vitamin coined
moments.body: Funk isolates an anti-beriberi compound and coins 'vitamine'.
moments.takeaway: Naming a class of molecules opens a research field.

moments.title: Vitamin C structure
moments.body: Vitamin C's structure is determined; it is the first vitamin to be artificially synthesised.
moments.takeaway: Chemistry caught up with nutrition slowly.

now.title: Nutrition today
now.body: Micronutrient deficiencies remain widespread in low-income countries. Fortified foods are public health tools.
now.open_questions: What hidden hungers persist in countries with abundant calories?

items.reflection: Hidden in the food we eat are molecules we only learned to name a century ago.

moments.title: First sliced bread sold
moments.body: Rohwedder's bread slicer enables Chillicothe Baking Company to sell sliced bread commercially.
moments.takeaway: Famous phrases ('best thing since sliced bread') have specific origins.

moments.title: Margarine fortified
moments.body: Margarine begins to be fortified with vitamin A and D to compensate for nutritional gaps.
moments.takeaway: Industrial food responded to nutritional critique with addition.

moments.title: Crisps in flavours
moments.body: Salt-and-vinegar and cheese-and-onion crisps become standard snack categories.
moments.takeaway: Snack food gave rise to new flavour engineering.

now.title: Convenience now
now.body: Meal kits, ready meals and delivery apps further reshape household food labour.
now.open_questions: How much further can food convenience go before becoming unsustainable?

items.reflection: Sliced bread saved households minutes; modern convenience saves hours.

moments.title: Spencer's melted chocolate
moments.body: Spencer notices a chocolate bar melting in his pocket near a magnetron, leading to the microwave oven patent.
moments.takeaway: Accidental observation can launch products.

moments.title: Compact countertop microwave
moments.body: Amana's Radarange brings the microwave under $500 and into kitchens.
moments.takeaway: Pricing and form factor determine domestic uptake.

moments.title: Ready-meal explosion
moments.body: Chilled ready meals expand around microwave reheating.
moments.takeaway: Appliances reshape food categories.

now.title: Microwave culture
now.body: Microwave penetration is near saturation in wealthy countries. Concerns over single-use containers persist.
now.open_questions: What is the next appliance to reshape kitchen labour?

items.reflection: An accident in front of a radar tube reshaped how households cook.

moments.title: The Jungle published
moments.body: Sinclair's novel exposes Chicago meatpacking conditions. Public outrage prompts the Pure Food and Drug Act.
moments.takeaway: Investigative literature can shape regulation directly.

moments.title: FDA precursor created
moments.body: The Food and Drug Administration's predecessor is established to enforce the new act.
moments.takeaway: Regulatory institutions follow scandals.

moments.title: HACCP developed
moments.body: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) is developed for astronaut food safety.
moments.takeaway: Space exploration drove modern food safety methodology.

now.title: Food safety now
now.body: HACCP underpins global food law. Whole-genome sequencing tracks outbreaks within days.
now.open_questions: How will food safety regulation handle decentralised digital marketplaces?

items.reflection: Food regulation often arrives by tragedy.

moments.title: Borlaug arrives in Mexico
moments.body: Borlaug starts breeding rust-resistant, high-yielding wheat in Mexico.
moments.takeaway: International agricultural research arose mid-century.

moments.title: India's wheat harvest
moments.body: India's wheat production grows fivefold over two decades using Borlaug's varieties.
moments.takeaway: Yield-focused crops staved off predicted famines.

moments.title: Borlaug wins Nobel Peace Prize
moments.body: Borlaug is credited with saving over a billion lives.
moments.takeaway: Agricultural science can win peace prizes.

now.title: Green Revolution legacy
now.body: Critics note increased water use, fertiliser dependence and farmer debt. The next green revolution may be biological.
now.open_questions: How do we feed 10 billion without further ecological damage?

items.reflection: Famines that did not happen are hard to remember.

moments.title: Speedee Service System
moments.who: Richard and Maurice McDonald, San Bernardino
moments.body: The McDonald brothers redesign their drive-in around assembly-line production.
moments.takeaway: Restaurants borrowed factory methods.

moments.title: Kroc's first franchise
moments.body: Kroc opens a franchise and later buys the company from the brothers.
moments.takeaway: Franchising scaled fast food globally.

moments.title: First McDonald's in Moscow
moments.body: 30,000 customers queue on opening day, a Cold War-era cultural moment.
moments.takeaway: Fast food became a soft-power symbol.

now.title: Fast food now
now.body: McDonald's serves over 60 million customers daily. Plant-based menus and delivery apps reshape the model.
now.open_questions: What replaces fast food as the default convenience meal?

items.reflection: What started in California suburbs now anchors towns worldwide.

moments.title: Dr. Atkins' Diet Revolution
moments.body: The low-carbohydrate diet is published and popularised, kicking off cycles of public dietary controversy.
moments.takeaway: Diet books shape national eating habits.

moments.title: Vegan Society founded
moments.body: Watson coins 'vegan' and founds the society.
moments.takeaway: Major dietary identities can be deliberately created.

moments.title: Mediterranean diet pyramid
moments.body: Willett and colleagues publish a Mediterranean dietary pyramid, embedding fish, olive oil and vegetables in mainstream nutrition advice.
moments.takeaway: Cultural eating patterns become research subjects.

now.title: Diets today
now.body: Intermittent fasting, plant-based eating and personalised nutrition compete for attention. Evidence quality remains highly variable.
now.open_questions: How should public health advise when individual evidence is weak?

items.reflection: Diet history is a cycle of new orthodoxies replacing old.

moments.title: EU 14 allergens regulation
moments.body: Regulation (EU) 1169/2011 requires labelling of 14 specified allergens in pre-packed and unpackaged food.
moments.takeaway: Standard allergen lists became a regulatory feature.

moments.title: Death of Natasha Ednan-Laperouse
moments.body: Natasha dies after eating a baguette without clear sesame labelling.
moments.takeaway: Regulatory gaps had personal consequences.

moments.title: Natasha's Law
moments.body: Pre-packed for direct sale food now requires full ingredient and allergen labelling.
moments.takeaway: Bereaved families have driven food labelling change.

now.title: Allergens now
now.body: Allergy prevalence is rising; oral immunotherapy is reaching clinical use.
now.open_questions: Can food labelling keep up with personalised dietary needs?

items.reflection: Food labels carry life-and-death information for some shoppers.

moments.title: Horsemeat detected
moments.body: DNA testing finds horsemeat in beef burgers sold across UK and Irish supermarkets.
moments.takeaway: Long supply chains can hide species substitution.

moments.title: Findus lasagne removed
moments.body: Findus beef lasagne is found to contain up to 100% horsemeat. Multiple retailers issue recalls.
moments.takeaway: Brand trust can collapse in days.

moments.title: Elliott Review
moments.body: Elliott's review recommends a UK Food Crime Unit, established 2015.
moments.takeaway: Food fraud became its own enforcement category.

now.title: Food fraud today
now.body: DNA-based testing, blockchain trials and supply-chain traceability are growing fields.
now.open_questions: Can supply chains ever be fully transparent at supermarket prices?

items.reflection: Cheap food has long supply chains and limited surveillance.

moments.title: Slow Food manifesto
moments.body: Petrini's Slow Food movement begins in response to a McDonald's opening near the Spanish Steps in Rome.
moments.takeaway: Cultural defence shaped a global food movement.

moments.title: University of Gastronomic Sciences
moments.body: The first university dedicated to gastronomy opens.
moments.takeaway: Food culture became a degree subject.

moments.title: EAT-Lancet Commission report
moments.body: The report proposes a 'planetary health diet' compatible with feeding 10 billion within environmental limits.
moments.takeaway: Scientific commissions now publish dietary policy.

now.title: Sustainable eating
now.body: School food procurement, food-system roadmaps and supply chain certification are policy frontiers.
now.open_questions: What makes a national food policy work?

items.reflection: Speed and slowness keep redefining what we mean by 'good food'.

moments.title: Irish Potato Famine
moments.body: Phytophthora infestans destroys potato crops; over a million die and a million emigrate.
moments.takeaway: Famine is political as much as biological.

moments.title: Bengal famine
moments.body: Up to 3 million die in Bengal as wartime policies disrupt rice supply.
moments.takeaway: Wartime priorities shape who eats.

moments.title: Yemen and Sudan crises
moments.body: Famine again threatens millions in conflict-affected regions.
moments.takeaway: Modern famines remain political events.

now.title: Food security now
now.body: The Global Hunger Index tracks chronic undernutrition. Climate, conflict and inflation interact.
now.open_questions: Can the global food system absorb climate shocks of the coming decades?

items.reflection: Famine has always been a question of distribution, not just yield.

moments.title: Flavr Savr tomato
moments.body: The first commercial GM food, a slow-ripening tomato, is approved by the FDA.
moments.takeaway: GM food entered the market with little public preparation.

moments.title: Golden Rice prototype
moments.body: Vitamin-A-enriched rice is developed to address childhood blindness in Asia.
moments.takeaway: Biotech can target nutritional deficits.

moments.title: Philippines approves Golden Rice
moments.body: After two decades of regulatory and public debate, Golden Rice is approved.
moments.takeaway: GM policy is slow even for humanitarian crops.

now.title: GM and gene editing
now.body: CRISPR-edited crops face different regulatory paths in different jurisdictions. UK Precision Breeding Act 2023 separates gene editing from transgenic GM.
now.open_questions: Where will gene-edited food regulation eventually settle?

items.reflection: Biotech promises and biotech distrust have been intertwined for 30 years.

moments.title: Maillard reaction described
moments.body: Maillard describes the browning reaction between amino acids and sugars during cooking.
moments.takeaway: Most cooked food owes its colour and flavour to this reaction.

moments.title: elBulli's innovations
moments.body: Adria pioneers spherification, foams and other techniques associated with molecular gastronomy.
moments.takeaway: Haute cuisine borrowed lab equipment.

moments.title: Bacon and egg ice cream
moments.body: The Fat Duck's signature dishes turn cookery into experimental science.
moments.takeaway: Television and restaurant innovation converged.

now.title: Food science today
now.body: Plant-based protein engineering and AI-driven recipe development continue the conversation between chemistry and the plate.
now.open_questions: What is the next molecular discovery to change cooking?

items.reflection: Cooking is one of the oldest applied chemistries.

moments.title: UK food rationing
moments.body: Wartime rationing extends for years after the war's end. National nutrition arguably improved.
moments.takeaway: Food policy can improve health under constraint.

moments.title: Free school milk
moments.body: Free milk for school children is introduced. Margaret Thatcher controversially ends it for older pupils in 1971.
moments.takeaway: School food has long been political.

moments.title: UK Sugar Tax
moments.body: The Soft Drinks Industry Levy prompts reformulation. Average sugar in soft drinks falls by 35% in two years.
moments.takeaway: Taxation can change food formulation faster than persuasion.

now.title: School food and policy
now.body: UK School Food Standards, free school meals expansion and Welsh universal primary free meals (2024) shape food access.
now.open_questions: Should all school meals be universally free?

items.reflection: Public food policy quietly shapes who eats well.

moments.title: Metchnikoff on probiotics
moments.body: Metchnikoff's 'The Prolongation of Life' argues fermented milk extends lifespan, popularising yogurt.
moments.takeaway: Functional food claims are over a century old.

moments.title: Japan's FOSHU system
moments.body: Japan creates a 'Foods for Specified Health Uses' category, a regulated functional food framework.
moments.takeaway: Regulatory frameworks can enable functional foods.

moments.title: EU health claims regulation
moments.body: Regulation 1924/2006 requires authorised health claims be scientifically substantiated.
moments.takeaway: Claim regulation followed market explosion.

now.title: Wellness foods now
now.body: Probiotics, adaptogens and 'functional' beverages drive supermarket categories. Evidence quality varies widely.
now.open_questions: How do we balance market freedom with scientific accuracy?

items.reflection: Today's wellness trends often have surprisingly old scientific roots.

moments.title: Columbian Exchange
moments.body: Tomatoes, potatoes, maize and chillies move east; wheat, sugar and livestock move west. Cuisines worldwide change.
moments.takeaway: What we think of as 'traditional' food is often a globalised mix.

moments.title: Tikka masala
moments.body: Chicken tikka masala, often claimed to have been invented in Glasgow, becomes a defining British dish.
moments.takeaway: National dishes are sometimes immigrant inventions.

moments.title: Sushi globalises
moments.body: Japanese cuisine becomes a global premium category, helped by refrigerated air freight.
moments.takeaway: Refrigeration logistics shape what we eat far from origin.

now.title: Global plates today
now.body: Ghost kitchens and delivery apps make global cuisines available in minutes.
now.open_questions: What does culinary authenticity mean in a globally remixed food world?

items.reflection: What we call our cuisine is often a recent settlement of older exchanges.

moments.title: Linde's ammonia compressor
moments.body: Linde patents an ammonia-based refrigeration cycle, replacing the natural ice trade.
moments.takeaway: Mechanical refrigeration was a 19th-century revolution.

moments.title: Domex Domelre refrigerator
moments.body: An early electric domestic refrigerator appears for sale in the US.
moments.takeaway: Domestic adoption took decades after invention.

moments.title: Montreal Protocol
moments.body: CFC refrigerants are phased out after the ozone layer crisis.
moments.takeaway: Refrigeration's history includes its planetary cost.

now.title: Cold chain today
now.body: Refrigeration accounts for around 1% of global CO2 emissions. Vaccine distribution depends on ultra-cold logistics.
now.open_questions: What replaces remaining HFC refrigerants?

items.reflection: What households take for granted has hidden energy and chemistry.

moments.title: Coca-Cola invented
moments.body: Pharmacist Pemberton creates a syrup originally including coca leaf and kola nut extracts.
moments.takeaway: Major brands often have pharmacy origins.

moments.title: Contour bottle
moments.body: The contour bottle is designed to be recognisable in the dark or shattered.
moments.takeaway: Packaging became part of the product identity.

moments.title: New Coke fails
moments.body: New Coke reformulation is reversed within 79 days after consumer backlash.
moments.takeaway: Brand loyalty can defeat market research.

now.title: Soft drinks today
now.body: Sugar taxes have triggered reformulation. Plant-based and functional beverages reshape the category.
now.open_questions: What is the next category-defining beverage?

items.reflection: Few brands have shaped 20th-century consumer culture as completely.
